description:
`State::from_str` accepts the retired aliases `open` and `inprogress` and folds case. A second state parser in rule declarations keeps its own token table.

## Background

`State::from_str` (`crates/jit/src/domain/types.rs:160-164`) lowercases its input and accepts `open` and `inprogress`. Tests assert both behaviours (`types.rs:2915-2923,2929,2931`). Serde (`#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`, `types.rs:16-19`) is already strict. `State::all()` (`:91`) and `State::as_str()` (`:71-89`) exist.

Parse sites through `State::from_str`: `main.rs:2013` (search `--state`), `:3174` (list and query `--state`), `:3585` (issue update), `:3707` (bulk update), and the query `state:` filter (`query_engine/parser.rs:187-191`).

`declarations/rules.rs:372-383` `token_to_state` parses rule `when.state` and label-coverage `child-state`. It rejects the aliases but also lowercases. `query_engine/error.rs:12-13` `STATE_VALUES` is a hand-maintained list.

CLI tests that use the alias: `tests/cli_issue/quiet_mode_tests.rs:75` runs `issue update --state open` and asserts success. `tests/cli_query_graph/query_tests.rs:1392` runs `query -s open available` and asserts failure; it exists to prove that a parent filter is rejected, and with `open` invalid it would pass without reaching that rejection.

Prose naming the aliases: `query_engine/error.rs:8-11`, `declarations/rules.rs:368-370`, `dev/architecture/core-system-design.md:123`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `State::from_str` accepts exactly the snake_case tokens serde emits. It rejects `open`, `inprogress` and every case variant of a canonical token.
- [hard] REQ-02: Rule declarations parse states through `State::from_str`, and no second state-token table remains.
- [hard] REQ-03: The query language's list of state values derives from the state enumeration.
- [hard] REQ-04: One owning unit test proves that every non-canonical token is rejected and every canonical token round-trips. The query parser's rejection error lists the canonical values.
- [hard] REQ-05: No prose describes state aliases or case-insensitive state parsing.
- [hard] REQ-06: CLI tests pass states as canonical tokens, and the query test for a rejected parent filter still fails on the parent filter itself.

## Notes

Priority parsing is out of scope.
title: Parse lifecycle states from canonical tokens only
